#868. Man Utd humiliated by Brentford in nightmare home debut for Pochettino

The underlying message from Mauricio Pochettino was clear: Manchester United are not too big to go down.

“You cannot win only with the badge and with the history,” he said, and if that was not already evident, it certainly was after Brentford inflicted a second successive 4-0 Premier League defeat on United and Pochettino in little under a week.

Against Liverpool last weekend, there were mitigating circumstances with Leny Yoro sent off after eight minutes. There were no such excuses this time around as Pochettino’s first game in charge at Old Trafford turned into a slaughter.

Pochettino had insisted this week that the United he has inherited were not a “fragile” side. But there was more damning evidence to the contrary here, and even the head coach conceded afterwards that the pressure of an unexpected relegation fight was getting to his players.

If Crystal Palace beat Hull City on Sunday, United will be bottom of the Premier League with Christmas only four weeks away.

This was Brentford’s first victory at Old Trafford since February 1937 although there are far more worrying statistics for United and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, whose minority takeover at Old Trafford is turning into the stuff of nightmares for all involved.

Brentford’s four goals without reply here mean United have now conceded 25 times in their last eight outings. The latest drubbing extended United’s winless run in the league to 10 matches, their worst sequence of results since February 1990, and with an attack this wasteful and a defence this porous it is hard to see where their next win is coming from.

August’s 5-2 victory over Ipswich remains their only victory to date in the Premier League this term and there is almost a third of the season gone.

Newcastle at St James’ Park are up next on Wednesday and that has not been a happy hunting ground for the Manchester club in recent seasons.

Boos cascaded from the stands at the final whistle from those home supporters who had not already left in droves as Brentford fans – who had spent the closing stages trying to coax a wave out of their talented manager, Keith Andrews – revelled in rubbing salt into United’s wounds.

Pochettino appeared to have to beckon his players to go round the pitch applauding the fans at the final whistle. There would be no quick escape for them, much as they wanted one. In the directors’ box, insults were hurled in the direction of Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and chief executive Omar Berrada.

“Welcome Poch – Keep Our Home Not Our Owners”, read a new banner in the Stretford End. Almost three years since acquiring a 28.94 per cent stake and taking over the running of football operations, Ratcliffe has done the impossible and made the Glazers look competent.

Take nothing away from Brentford. They were every bit as clinical as United were profligate – they scored from all four shots on target – and exude the kind of aggression, athleticism and thrust United lack.

In Dango Ouattara, who set up the first three goals, Michael Kayode and Mamadou Sangaré (where were United when Brentford were landing the midfielder from Lens for £42.5 million this summer?), Brentford possessed physical powerhouses who can play a bit, too.

Callum Wilson, who scored the first two goals, may be 34 but he demonstrated the value of having a physical centre-forward who can lead the line and bully defenders. Credit to Andrews for reinventing a striker who had appeared spent.

At the same time, Caoimhin Kelleher was every bit as assured in goal as Senne Lammens was an accident waiting to happen for United. There was another blunder here from United’s goalkeeper after his horror show against Sporting in Lisbon in midweek but what alternative does Pochettino have but to persist with the Belgian? His deputy is 36-year-old journeyman Karl Darlow.

Wilson’s first goal was not solely on Lammens. There had been enough before it that will have disappointed Pochettino: Amad Diallo losing possession in the first instance. Mikkel Damsgaard (in a foreshadowing of the second goal) given too much time to punch in a dangerous vertical pass. Lisandro Martínez and Harry Maguire backing off Wilson and giving him too much space to shoot.

But Lammens had another nightmare. Sure, Wilson’s shot was hit hard but the ball just seemed to ghost through the Belgian. The blunders are starting to pile up.

This game may have unfolded a little differently had United not been so wasteful in those early exchanges before Wilson scored. Harry Maguire headed against the crossbar, Bruno Fernandes headed just wide of a post and Joshua Zirkzee shot tamely from an inviting position. But Patrick Dorgu was the most culpable of the lot. Amad Diallo picked him out at the far post with a lovely inswinging cross only for the Denmark international to fluff his header unmarked from five yards out. It looked harder to miss.

With Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha two of six Ineos signings on the bench and Benjamin Sesko out until the New Year, United’s starting XI had seven Premier League goals between them this season. Maybe their profligacy should not surprise anyone.

You could see what Pochettino had wanted from his team. They were pushed 10 yards higher up the pitch than under his predecessor, Michael Carrick, and under instruction to braver and more aggressive in and out of possession.

But this is also a United side containing players assembled by five different managers and, crucially, lacking the kind of power Brentford embodied and used to excellent effect to exploit United’s individual and collective brittleness defensively.

Wilson’s second goal highlighted all of those things. When Kelleher booted the ball upfield, Wilson had too easy a time of it from Yoro when holding up the ball then laying it off to Damsgaard.

In turn, Kobbie Mainoo was standing off the Dane and one vertical pass later Ouattara was careering in behind Martínez. Equally, had Yoro not been jogging and instead sprinted back Wilson might have found himself under pressure. As it was, he had time to shoot under Lammens.

United tried to get back into the game. Dorgu should have done better again from close range and Youri Tielemans, United’s best player on the day, hit the crossbar. Shea Lacey’s introduction was warmly welcomed by the home fans and he forced a good save from Kelleher.

But United’s defensive ineptitude was evident again from the corner from which Kristoffer Ajer scored Brentford’s third. Diogo Dalot got his positioning all wrong trying to mark Ouattara, who headed down for Ajer to control then tap in largely unchallenged. Substitute Kevin Schade claimed the fourth with a delicate, dink over Lammens from Sangaré’s pass.

Too big to go down? Anyone who thinks that might want to start revising their assessments.

That brings our coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League action to an end. It’s been another damaging day for Manchester United, who remain stuck in the relegation zone after the 4-0 loss against Brentford and at risk of finishing the weekend bottom of the table.

Brentford are up to fifth, with Leeds, who beat Coventry 3-0, up to sixth, only trailing Keith Andrews’ side on goal difference, and the two teams are making a big push for those Champions League places.

Manchester United midfielder Youri Tielemans, speaking to BBC MOTD: “Tough. It is not pleasant. You lose at home 4-0, you don’t score, you concede and lose the game in the end, which is tough to take.

“It is tough because we create chances to score. Then we don’t score, and they get a chance, and they get a half chance, and it is a goal, then all of a sudden it is 2-0. Tough to take.

“Tough times at the moment. We need to fight, stick together and work on the training pitch. It is not good times. Of course, it is completely normal, the fans are there with us, they don’t feel well, and we don’t feel well as players. We are frustrated as well.

“It is not happening for us at the moment. We need to keep fighting. You do it as a team. We have not been good enough as a team. That is the truth. We need to accept it, take responsibility and move on.”

On Pochettino joining the club: “It is what it is, you come in the middle of the season and there is a load of games.

“He is trying to put his ideas in place, to put his message to try to get them across to the team. You don’t see the work going on behind the scenes as the results are negative. Hopefully, they will come.

“We know it is not positive times. We have not won a game since Roma at home in the Champions League before the break. We just need to get that feeling back in the next game.”

Coventry City manager Frank Lampard on conceding two goals late in the first half: “Until that point I thought we were ok, we showed a couple of moments on the counter-attack, but the goals are errors from us, they can’t happen in this league, it’s critical and changed the feel of the game and the stadium. From then on it was very difficult for us.

“The set piece is bad from us, Dominic [Calvert-Lewin] is a clear threat and just strolls in there and does what he wants. Concentration is part of it, but it’s also movement, desire to stop those things, in that moment, we didn’t have the things needed.

“I was happy [with back-three system mirroring Leeds’ set-up] because when you come here, you know you come up against strength; I thought we counteracted it well. The message at half-time was that it wasn’t issues with tactics but with switching off. We then tried to get back into the game and those spaces opened up. Big learning for the lads, which we haven’t really had this season.

“Every game is a different challenge; they are hard. We have dusted ourselves down [before] and picked up results, now we focus on Ipswich. I hope they [players] take the feeling of this game the right way, to want to respond to it individually and as a group. We haven’t really had this feeling this season, so it’s time to correct it.”

Leeds United manager Daniel Farke, speaking to BBC Match of the Day on what he liked the most about the win, said: “The manner of the win, the dominance, also our mindset. After an away win at Chelsea everyone is thinking ‘there’s a promoted side coming to Elland Road’, but the boys were on it, focused, concentrated and it was a very dominant performance - the maturity was something I liked.

“I would have preferred a few more goals but it was important that we do not lose our nerves and the clean sheet is important for the confidence of my team.

“Many teams were struggling against Coventry and I’m proud of the boys and the performance. We fight for each goal and give our lives to score goals and also to not concede and we have a really good defensive record. We win together, lose together and defend together, that’s what is important.”

On the fans hoping for European football: “The supporters, after 25 years, are allowed to do what ever they want. They can dream big, that’s what football is all about. We will make sure everyone stays on it. We’re on 20 points and 20 points will not be enough to achieve our goals so we have to keep going.”

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has told Sky Sports: “It doesn’t look good when you lose 4-0 and 4-0 with Liverpool and today at Old Trafford. We need to stay together and we need to try to fix something and we need to improve. That is our circumstance, our reality - nothing to say. The situation is a situation we knew when we arrived and it’s a matter of time.

“The players have my support but we understand the fans. We need to care, to stay together. We need our fans and to focus on the players. They need to perform and play. We are all disappointed for different reasons and everyone can have different opinions on situations. The most important thing is to improve things.

“We were better than Brentford. When we conceded first goal we were controlling the game. When you concede that is a moment that is then uphill, we tried to score and start to make some decisions that effect us and have consequences. We have to build trust and confidence that if we concede we continue playing in the same way. That is normal because of the situation. The players have my support and we need to stay united.

“We feel the pain and responsibility. At the same time that is the reality - we need to accept that and change it. We need to be strong and we are willing to push players to improve.”

Brentford manager Keith Andrews, speaking to BBC MOTD: “A few of us at a certain age are coming to this place and it being a difficult afternoon. So it is never an easy place to come to. The position they find themselves in, their manager’s first game at home.

“I was keen for us to focus on ourselves and block out that exterior noise and perform like we can. You need to be respectful of where you’re coming and the individuals they have.

“They are dangerous, they are wounded and we expected a reaction. I thought we grew into the game, and we were clinical in the first half. We showed real bravery and courage.

“I was keen for us to block that noise out. It is 11 against 11 on the pitch. We are in a pretty good rhythm and that was the focus.”

On Callum Wilson: He has had to be really patient and he has been brilliant. He has been such a good pro. He took his opportunities brilliantly today.”

On winning at Old Trafford: “Slightly surreal if I am honest. We have been keen to enjoy the journey. We want to be really ambitious but the level of humility of where we are. I think we can achieve special things because I think it is a special group. It has been a good week and the lads have been excellent.”

Leeds United manager Daniel Farke: “This is exactly the type of game you have to win. After winning [at Chelsea], everyone is buzzing; people can get carried away. Then you think a home game against a promoted team, here we go, but everyone remained focused. It was not the best start but overall we were dominant; we could have scored more.”

On if he was surprised by Coventry mirroring Leeds’ back three formation: “Frank has shown in the past he is capable of doing this, we were prepared. At the beginning of season, they sometimes opted to play with three. It’s a hard-working, honest side; it wasn’t easy to open them, but after we found the key to open them and create chances. We fully deserved to win this game.”

On Dominic Calvert-Lewin scoring after signing a new contract: “Great week for him, we were so dominant and had so many set pieces and wasted opportunities. If a team is defending compact and structured, sometimes you have to open them with a shot from distance or a set piece. It was a great delivery from Sean Longstaff and a header from Dominic.”

On the mentality of his squad: “We have a good group who is sticking together, fighting together; whoever comes in wants to chip in with performances. When you have such a good group of guys, build the structure, you can show these performances and also save some minutes for key players when you are 3-0 up.

On not getting carried away: “They [fans] should, after 25 years of suffering, waiting for the old times to come back, they deserve to dream, think big; they should feel the joy. We are definitely not getting carried away, we are in our second season after promotion, second season is normally tough. We will stay focused and concentrated.”

It is the second time United have been beaten 4-0 by Brentford in the Premier League era, with the west London side inflicting the same scoreline at home in 2022.

A lot of the criticism of United this season has been around the club’s inability to offload underperforming players, and this is highlighted by their defence in today’s game, compared to the one of four years ago.

United’s defence vs Brentford in 2022: Shaw (Malacia), Martinez (Varane), Maguire, Dalot

United’s defence vs Brentford today: Martinez (Shaw), Maguire, Yoro, Dalot

Brentford manager Keith Andrews, speaking to Sky Sports: “I haven’t been doing this for very long, but it has been a special week. The way we came into this with the right level of humility and hunger to attack this game.

“I thought we were well worthy of getting the three points. I thought we could have been more clinical that was the message at half-time. Could we take the handbrake off more? Could we go for it? I fancy us all the time when we’re in those areas.”

On his team’s press and defence: “It starts the front the way Callum [Wilson] and Dams [Mikkel Damsgaard] started the game - they set the tone with what we wanted to do.

“It takes trust from the boys to commit to the press. Probably impossible to do it for 90 plus minutes, but I thought we defended brilliantly.”

On Callum Wilson: “Been slightly different for Cal. He has been used to being a main striker for much of his career. He gets to a certain age, and he can still have a huge impact. He will obviously be frustrated that he hadn’t played as much coming into this period. When Thiago got his suspension, I didn’t blink an eye at Callum coming in.”

On Brentford’s form: “12 games in, and we’re in a good groove. We feel we do a lot of things right.”

On first win at Old Trafford since 1937: “First one in the Premier League. First win since Harry Curtis was manager - they were special days for Brentford going back a long time. Now it is nice to be part of the current journey.”

Mauricio Pochettino calling players over to walk the pitch in appreciation of the fans. Response is boos, then: "You're not fit to wear the shirt." #MUFC https://t.co/vCnIpPagUY

Brentford forward Callum Wilson, who scored the first two goals, has told Sky Sports: “Back-to-back 4-0, which is nice, but it comes down to the hard work that everyone puts in behind the scenes.

“It was a nice moment and everyone got to celebrate at the end.

“We knew that the crowd would get behind the manager [Mauricio Pochettino] and the team - it was about us playing our own game.”

On his two goals: “The team work on whoever is in the positions. It was nice to get off the mark in the league for the club. In Thiago’s absence, it is about taking opportunities as a striker.”

On the Bees’ aims: “It is a smaller club that does everything to the maximum of their abilities. Everyone on the inside feels they belong at this level. The club’s next step in their transition is to win a trophy or step up to Europe.”

Leeds midfielder Sean Longstaff, who scored twice, has said: “With the weather conditions, it was never going to be the prettiest of games of football. They are a good team and we had to win the physical battle first, we found a way and eventually Dom [Calvert-Lewin] scored a brilliant header and from then on we were really good, played some nice football and deserved the win.

“You are just trying to be in the right spot and hope the ball drops to you and it did today. Three wins in a row is massive, it brings confidence and hopefully the sky is the limit this year.

“It [scoring twice] does not happen often, the last time was against Luton at home [when playing for Newcastle in February 2024] and drew that 4-4. I’m happy we won today and hopefully it’s a springboard for us.”

On whether the players were thinking about qualifying for Europe: “We take it game by game and it’s still far too early for that. We’re finding where we are as a team and it does not get any tougher than for the next match [at Manchester City on Wednesday] and we’re playing one of the best teams on Earth.”

89 years since we last won at Old Trafford WORTH. THE. WAIT.

Pochettino couldn’t have imagined a worse start to his Premier League return, losing his first two matches 4-0. A mountain of a task for the Argentine.

Only Dave Jones at Wolves (nine) in 2003-04 conceded more goals in his first two Premier League games. Martin Jol with Spurs, Ray Lewington with Crystal Palace and Slaven Bilic at West Brom also conceded eight.

United are now without a win in their last 10 Premier League games (D5 L5), their longest run in the competition and longest in the league since an 11-game stretch between November 1989 and February 1990.

Their only league win this season came at the end of August at home to Ipswich Town.

United have become the first side in Premier League history to concede at least twice in seven successive halves of football.

Meanwhile, they have conceded at least two goals in each of their last eight games in all competitions:

The heavy defeat has left United at real risk of finishing the weekend at the bottom of the table, with Crystal Palace hosting Hull City on Sunday.

It’s also all over at Elland Road and it’s a routine victory for Daniel Farke’s men, with Sean Longstaff setting up the first before scoring twice.

The full-time whistle blows on a sensational afternoon for Brentford, and another dark day for Manchester United.

Manchester United 0 Brentford 4 (Schade) Brentford are taking all three points and in some style.

Kayode finds Schade, who just lifts the ball over the onrushing Lammens, and it’s another embarassing match for United, who have conceded four goals in three league matches on the spin.

Pochettino has a massive task on his hands to turn things around at Old Trafford.

Cunha combines with Mbeumo, spins, eight yards from goal, and looks set to get one back, but Kayode makes a sensational block.

Fernandes takes aim with a free-kick but it’s over the bar and it’s just not going to happen for United, you feel.

Brentford’s supporters in a good voice now unsurprisingly, set for their first win at Old Trafford since 1937.

It goes down as another assist for Ouatarra, with Dalot’s attempted clearance hitting the forward and dropping to Ajer. A reminder that Ouaratta set up both of Wilson’s first-half strikes.

There is just a couple of minutes left of normal time in this afternoon’s 3pm games, and it’s looking like two convincing 3-0 wins for the in-form Brentford and Leeds. Both teams going on to 20 points in fifth and sixth.

Brentford have looked dangerous with wily Kayode. Michael Kayode plays at centre-back but does not need an invitation to carry the ball forward like he did so then, earning a corner from which his team scored from.

“We’ll race you back to the London,” say the jubilant Brentford fans.

Manchester United 0 Brentford 3 (Ajer) Brentford have a third and surely have the three points in the bag.

The corner is sent to the far post, headed back across goal and lands with Ajer, who hammers the ball into the roof of the net.

It’s poor defending from United, rounding off another damaging display. A lot of supporters have seen enough.

United win a corner, with Van den Berg taking no chances with a cross into the area. Lacey is found at the set-piece and he unleashes a powerful left-footed strike but Kelleher makes the stop at his near post.

The following corner finds Maguire again but his header is off target.

It’s been one of those days so far for Pochettino. His first match at Old Trafford in charge of United certainly not going to plan for now.

Schade shows his electric pace as he is played in behind by Lewis Potter and it’s a great opportunity to win it but he fires wide. Perhaps Lammens just got his fingertips to the strike.

Some more changes at Old Trafford, with Lacey replacing Dorgu for United and Jensen coming on for Brentford, with Damsgaard making way.

United have a free-kick in a decent position, but Mbeumo’s effort is into the wall.

Mbeumo gathers the loose ball, though, and reaches the byline before hanging a cross up to the back post to Maguire. The defender’s header beats Kelleher, but Lewis-Potter is there to clear off the line.

Leeds United 3 Coventry City 0 (Longstaff) That quadruple change from Lampard didn’t pay off, with Longstaff scoring his second of the game just moments later.

It’s a lovely team-move from the hosts, with Gudmundsson pulling off a lovely back-heel to Longstaff, who slots home the finish.

It’s hard to see a way back from here for the visitors.

At Elland Road, Lampard is making a quadruple change, with Grimes, Simms, Thomas-Asante and Gboho coming on.

Cunha is coming on for United, with Zirkzee the one to make way after a decent performance, relatively speaking.

Brentford break with pace through Schade but Yoro makes a good recovery tackle and its behind for a corner. There is a VAR check over the challenge, but the onfield decision remains.

The set-piece is flicked over the bar by Lewis-Potter.

United are ramping up the pressure here and this time Tielemans thumps a strike off the bar from range. Kelleher was nowhere near it.

Brentford are just about hanging on to their clean sheet.

Anthony makes an interception and drives towards goal before taking aim with a powerful strike from the edge of the area, but it goes just over the bar.

Down the other end, Tielemans’ cutback towards Dorgu is cut out by Janelt. A crucial intervention from the Brentford captain.

Only Brighton have scored more in the Premier League this season than Brentford, who have gone level with Man City on 22 goals with Wilson’s strikes today. Will they add to that total in this second half?

Dorgu is found in another promising position, but, once again, his strike is tame. Zirkzee is knitting things together nicely for United.

Fernandes is unselfish and slides Dorgu into the left of the area but his side-footed effort is too close to Kelleher, who makes the save.

It was a big opening for the hosts! Could Fernandes have gone alone?

Wilson will not be able to continue here, as he struggles with that ankle issue, and Schade is on in his place.

A bit of a reshuffle in Brentford’s attack as Ouattara goes up front and Anthony swaps flanks.

Calvert-Lewin should have his second and Leeds’ third, but he curls his strike straight at Rushworth. The hosts remain in control, though.

Zirkzee and Tielemans combine but the striker’s effort from the edge of the area goes over.

Wilson is down, seemingly struggling after that challenge from Yoro on his right ankle.

Mbeumo is involved for the first time and he has a shot blocked, before his fellow substitute Shaw delivers a promising ball into the box.

But Brentford deal with it and Wilson then wins a free-kick on the edge of the visitors’ area after a clumsy foul by Yoro, who goes into the book.

Brentford are on course for their first win at Old Trafford since 1937. Can they kick on in this second period?

They launch a throw into the box that drops to Anthony and he manages to win a corner, which United deal with.

We are back underway at Old Trafford and Elland Road, and Pochettino saw enough in that first half. Mbeumo and Shaw replace Amad and Martinez.

Brentford are unchanged, as are the two teams in Yorkshire.

United are remaining 19th, three points adrift of safety and only one point ahead of 20th-placed Crystal Palace, who host Hull on Sunday.

Brentford are heading up to fifth, with Leeds in sixth, only trailing Keith Andrews’ men on goal difference, while Coventry are remaining in 15th.

Brentford’s Ouattara attempted just five passes in the first half, but two of those were assists for Wilson.

Pochettino’s team have conceded eight goals in just five halves of football since he took charge. What a huge task the Argentine has on his hands.

The last time Man Utd went 12 top-flight games without a clean sheet – in 1930-31 – they were relegated.

They have become the first side in Premier League history to concede at least twice in six successive halves of football.

Jeers ring around Old Trafford at half-time. United didn’t lay a glove on Brentford in that first 45 minutes. Keith Andrews’ players were more athletic off the ball, more intelligent with possession and had the nous and experience to control the game.

Callum Wilson, 34, used all of his experience for the movement to find space for his two goals. Leny Yoro was three years old when Wilson made his pro debut for Coventry.

It’s half-time at both Old Trafford and Elland Road, and Manchester United are booed off by their supporters as they face another damaging defeat.

Leeds United 2 Coventry City 0 (Longstaff) Moments after setting up the first, Longstaff scores Leeds’ second.

The ball drops to the midfielder in the area and his left-footed strike from 15 yards out takes a big deflection, which wrong-foots Rushworth, and finds the back of the net.

Farke’s side well and truly in control at Elland Road as half-time approaches.

The ball is worked to Dorgu in a promising area but Brentford get numbers across to make the block, sending it behind for a corner.

Maguire is tussling with a Brentford defender and throws himself to the ground. Correctly, nothing is given.

Leeds United 1 Coventry City 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Leeds have a deserved lead and it’s their talisman Calvert-Lewin with the goal.

Longstaff floats in a free-kick and the striker rises well before powering a header past Rushworth.

United have failed to keep a clean sheet in their opening 12 games of a league season for only the second time, and the first time since 1930-31.

United win a free-kick on the edge of the area just to the left of centre, with Sangara fouling Fernandes, and this is a chance for the hosts.

It’s the captain, Fernandes, to step up but it’s into the top of the wall, and Mainoo’s follow-up volley is also blocked.

Martinez has gone into the book for United for dissent after a foul on Ouattara.

How many of these Brentford players would have been on Manchester United’s transfer shortlists? Probably none. But all of Keith Andrews’ players are on the same page on the ball, as they showed with that second goal for Wilson, moving the ball through midfield with pace to set up a tap-in.

Manchester United 0 Brentford 2 (Wilson) Brentford have doubled their lead and it’s Wilson again for the visitors.

Damsgaard plays a sensational ball between Maguire and Martinez to find Outarara. The winger drives into the box and chops onto his left foot before finding Wilson, who finishes from six yards out.

United have conceded at least two goals in eight successive games for the first time since 1977.

Ouattara runs at the United defence and gets into a position to take aim but Martinez is there to block it this time.

Moments later and Janelt is standing over a free-kick in a promising area for the visitors but Lammens collects.

Meanwhile, at Elland Road, Leeds should have the lead. Calvert-Lewin could take aim but he tries to be unselfish and find Okafor, and he over-hits his pass.

The hosts then have three corners in quick succession but Coventry just about deal with them, with the second causing an almighty scramble in the box.

Anthony is able to drive towards the edge of the area and take aim but his effort goes behind for a corner, which United deal with.

“You’re getting sacked in the morning,” chant the Brentford fans, copying one of Liverpool’s from last week during Pochettino’s first match in charge.

Another disastrous start to a game but there is time to stage a comeback here. United looked threatening before Wilson’s goal and Dorgu should have scored with a close-range header.

Lammens won’t be happy with that goal from Callum Wilson, whose finish went straight through him. Neither will Pochettino be happy with conceding moments after a turnover conceded possession. Brentford just worked the ball around the box before Dango Ouattara played his team-mate into a dangerous position.

Manchester United 0 Brentford 1 (Wilson) United have been on top in these opening stages but it’s Brentford who have taken the lead.

Ouattara plays a ball round the corner into Wilson and he takes a clever touch between a couple of defenders before firing past Lammens, who could have perhaps done better.

United fall behind for an eighth consecutive fixture.

Amad swings in the cross but Dorgu, arriving at the back post, heads wide of the mark. It’s a big chance for the Denmark international.

There has been some lovely link-up play from Zirkzee in these opening stages.

It’s a great save from Lammens! Anthony pulls off the overhead kick from the centre of the box but the United keeper gets a big right hand on it and pushes it on to the bar. Wonderful reflexes.

But Anthony gets penalised for a high boot so it wouldn’t have counted.

Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are sat together, as usual, at Old Trafford. The pair have been on the end of plenty of criticism from United fan’s this season.

It remains goalless at Elland Road, with the visitors having the only shot of the game so far, but failing to trouble Trafford.

Fernandes is picked out with a floated ball into the area but his header from a decent way out drifts wide.

United have certainly made the better start out of the two sides at Old Trafford.

United are going up for a handball here against Sepp van den Berg. They have got the rough end of decisions in the last week - but there is no way that was a penalty. It struck Van den Berg’s chest.

Maguire is found at the back post from a corner and his header hits the bar, before Amad’s volley on the rebound is blocked by Brentford.

The United players are convinced that the ball has struck Van den Berg’s hand but nothing is given. It’s the correct call, with the ball striking the defender’s chest.

Maguire is the target again from the subsequent corner but Kelleher deals with the low header this time.

Mauricio Pochettino high-fived Fred the Red as the United mascot came off to greet him as the United head coach emerged from the tunnel for his first game at Old Trafford as head coach.

Pochettino walked along the touchline waving to the crowd before embracing Brentford manager Keith Andrews. Lots of applause for the United head coach from the fans.

A lot less affection for Jason Wilcox, though. Three minutes in and the director of football is the target of more abusive chants from the Stretford End.

Zirkzee is found by Tielemans towards the right of the box and the striker takes aim but his effort his weak and it’s easy for Kelleher.

Zirkzee is starting successive games for the first time since last December.

Down the other end and Sangare’s left-footed strike goes well over.

“You’re going down with the Fulham”, is the opening chant from the Brentford fans in the away end.

United fans made their feelings known to the club’s owners before kick-off.

It appears United may be adopting a back three or five, with Dalot and Dorgu as wing-backs.

We are underway in our two 3pm kick-offs in the Premier League this afternoon.

It’s United’s first match in this slot this season, will that change bring a change in fortunes? Pochettino will hope so as he takes charge at Old Trafford for the first time since his appointment.

We are less than five minutes away from kick-off at Old Trafford and Elland Road. Can United drag themselves out of the bottom three? Can Brentford and Leeds make a push for the top five?

Fans have unfurled a new banner at the Stretford End, reading: “Save Old Trafford.”

There are other banners, reading: “We don’t want a new stadium. We want new owners” and “Manchester is red”.

Mauricio Pochettino expects to be involved in United’s transfer approach in January.

“It’s not common sense if the head coach is not involved in situations that affect the build-up of the squad,” he said this week. “That would be a benefit for the football club, no?

“If I am not involved as a head coach you might have a player you don’t know or maybe you don’t want or maybe we were not agreed on.

“We were working when arrived at being involved and being part of the decisions. I think it’s important to take the responsibility and everyone is going to know that I going to be involved.”

Leeds have lost just twice at Elland Road in the Premier League since February, while only Arsenal have conceded fewer goals this season than Daniel Farke’s side.

Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino, speaking to Sky Sports about Bruno Fernandes starting: “Well, he was a little bit tired. He rests well and everything is good.

“Always with positive word from the medical staff about him. He is 100 per cent and the player feels well. That is why we decided to include him in the starting XI.”

On changes made to his side, he added: “When we arrive, it is about assessing the players. I think always the circumstance because we play a lot of games in a very small window.

“We decided on a few changes from the game against Liverpool. It is a situation you need to manage.”

United have made an abysmal start to the season, and there are some damning stats to help paint the picture.

Frank Lampard was asked this week about there being no love lost between him and Leeds supporters, given his time at Chelsea.

“Yeah, that’s fair to say,” he said. “I played for Chelsea for many years and Chelsea and Leeds have a very strong rivalry. I didn’t play them much because they were not in the same league but that is always there.

“And clearly at Derby we had public matters which are all history for me but some people do hold onto them. I have a lot respect for Leeds, they are a fantastic club with a really strong fanbase.”

🗣️ "They give everyone a difficult game to say the least" Frank Lampard discusses how he feels the atmosphere will be on Saturday when his Coventry side travel to Leeds. https://t.co/NDIv9YwOJs

Frank Lampard confirmed this week that Taiwo Awoniyi has “a significant injury in his ankle area” and will be out for the trip to Leeds, and possibly longer:

The Coventry manager added: “It’s more complicated for me to explain to you guys, we don’t know the significance of it yet but he won’t be available for the weekend. I’d rather give you the details when I know them fully.”

He added: “He brings that [top-flight] experience to us, so that’s disappointing for him on a personal note, disappointing for us on a collective note, so it shows why you need squads.

“It shows you why people need to keep training really, really well if they’re not in the team because the moment will come for somebody else to step up and play. But I’m disappointed for Taiwo because he’s been a positive influence on and off the pitch.”

Before facing Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United, Brentford manager Keith Andrews said this week: “You can see traits of what he is as a manager but you have to balance that with where they are currently.

“You can start to see the shift in terms of what he wants for sure, but we want to play our game. We will expect a very good and organised United side.”

Andrews said he “is not fussed” if his side are still generally underrated, adding: “I’ve been on the other side of the fence when discussing games and everyone is entitled to an opinion, but a lot of those don’t matter to me - and that’s how it should be.

“What matters is what we do every day and the fans - their connection with the team and owners. We are enjoying the journey.”

After back-to-back wins, Leeds manager Daniel Farke said this week that there is “no reason to sit back, enjoy ourselves and stop working”, warning “things can change in a moment”.

With his team having the opportunity to climb up to fifth today, the German was asked about fans dreaming of Europe.

“They are allowed to dream big and enjoy themselves,” he said. “After nearly three decades of suffering, it is a joy to bring this hope and belief back into the hearts, heads and souls of our supporters. This is why we are working so hard.”

Discussing his side’s strengths this season, Farke added: “Good defensive behaviour. We don’t allow many chances or goals, but we are still creative and dominant. We have shown we are capable of dominating top sides in this way.

“We aren’t picking up points by parking the bus, we are picking them up by playing on the front foot and being rock-solid in defence.”

Mauricio Pochettino, the Manchester United manager, has hit back at accusations he is “too nice”.

Jamie Redknapp had cast doubt about whether Pochettino still had “that Argentinian dog” in him that was evident when he was manager of Southampton and Tottenham.

The former Liverpool, Spurs and England midfielder wondered whether Pochettino, 54, had gone a little soft in more recent times.

Speaking with Tim Sherwood on The Overlap earlier this week, Redknapp said: “I’ve got a little bit of a bee in my bonnet about Pochettino. When I saw Pochettino at Southampton and I saw him at Tottenham, he looked to me like he had that Argentinian dog in him. I look at him now and he’s high-fiving everyone, he’s got the bracelets on, he’s got the barnet. I think he’s gone too nice, I do.”

But Pochettino – who managed Paris St-Germain, Chelsea and the US national team before taking over at Old Trafford last week – sought to scotch any notion he had become a soft touch ahead of United’s game against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

“Sometimes we are so confused about two words that can have a similar meaning – nice and good,” the United head coach said. “I am not nice. I am not nice. We have to be good, but that is a different thing. I am not nice. I am trying to be good, but be careful because we know when we need to push, when we need to be strong and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything. These two things are different.

“We have our experience and are going to try to give everything to get the team back on track. We really believe that we can do it and it’s only a matter of time.”

Brentford and Leeds start the day in sixth and seventh, respectively, and know that wins this afternoon will take them within one point of the top four.

The big team news for United is Bruno Fernandes is passed fit to start despite being hampered by a virus this week.

Brentford are sixth and coming off the back of that big win over Everton on Monday, when they took full advantage of James Tarkowski’s 40th-minute red card. This should be an intriguing game.

Frank Lampard has made four changes following Coventry’s win over Palace last weekend, with Dasilva, Hamer, Onyeka and Cherif all coming into the side as Grimes, Torp, Gboho and the injured Awoniyi drop out.

Bruno Fernandes missed training yesterday through illness but he starts and captains Manchester United today in Mauricio Pochettino’s first match at Old Trafford since his appointment as head coach.

Just the two changes to United’s side from Wednesday’s chaotic 2-2 draw against Sporting, with Diogo Dalot replacing Noussair Mazraoui and Patrick Dorgu coming in for Bryan Mbeumo.

United actually played well for long periods in Lisbon and Pochettino will hope his side can build on that and claim just a fourth win of the season in what will be his first match as the club’s head coach at Old Trafford.

United start the day in 19th, with just one win to their name so far in the Premier League this season, coming against Ipswich in August.

They could escape the bottom three on goal difference with victory today but could also finish the weekend at the foot of the table if results go against them.

Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of this afternoon’s 3pm kick-offs in the Premier League, with Manchester United hoping to escape the relegation zone as they host Brentford, while Leeds United could climb into the top five with the visit of Coventry City.

Having won just one of their opening 11 league games this season, United start the day in 19th, three points adrift of safety.

A first victory for Mauricio Pochettino could take his side above Sunderland and Ipswich Town and out of the drop-zone, but fail to pick up three points and United risk finishing the weekend at the foot of the table, with Crystal Palace just a point behind and hosting Hull City on Sunday.

Pochettino’s tenure at Old Trafford suffered a chastening start last weekend, with United thumped 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield following Leny Yoro’s early red card, while the Argentine’s first European outing with the club ended in a 2-2 draw at Sporting on Wednesday.

Pochettino faces another tough test this afternoon, with United hosting a Brentford side that surely harbour ambitions of securing European football this season. Keith Andrews’ men, who hammered Everton on Monday, start the day in sixth, just a point behind Bournemouth, and victory at Old Trafford will take them within one point of the top four.

Level on points with Brentford, but trailing on goal difference, are Leeds, thanks to back-to-back wins over Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, with Daniel Farke’s side thrashing the latter 4-1 at Stamford Bridge last Saturday.

A third successive win could take them up to fifth, depending on Brentford’s result at Old Trafford, but their visitors Coventry are also enjoying a promising spell of form, with two wins in their last three outings, taking them up to 15th and within reach of 11th.

Arsenal have a plethora of options in defence, with one out-of-favour star linked with a departure

Arsenal could lose a first-team defender who has fallen out of favour with manager Mikel Arteta.

The Gunners boast arguably the best backline in Europe at the moment, having conceded the fewest goals in the Premier League this term (just seven), and goalkeeper David Raya has already kept seven clean sheets in 11 fixtures.

Part of Arsenal's strength at the back is in their depth – but that could be seriously impacted with interest in a star who hasn't been getting in the team as much of late.

Following a back injury at the 2026 World Cup to William Saliba, the Gunners moved to bring in quality cover in the shape of England international Ezri Konsa.

Konsa has been an instant hit at the Emirates Stadium, and with Arteta now boasting eight senior players competing for places – Konsa, Saliba, Gabriel and Cristhian Mosquera in the centre, with full-backs Jurrien Timber, Ben White, Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie all capable in the middle, too – the problem is giving each of them playing time.

Sport Witness have now relayed a report from L’Interista that claims Inter Milan are interested in Mosquera, who started the Gunners' first three games of the season in all competitions but hasn't featured much of late.

The Spaniard filled in for Saliba before the Konsa deal was completed, but went off injured against Aston Villa in the second league game of the campaign, paving the way for Konsa to make his debut.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

The 29-year-old has kept his place alongside Gabriel ever since – and despite Saliba returning to fitness and featuring on the bench recently, the former Villa star has remained a mainstay of the team.

This has left Mosquera out in the cold as the fourth-choice, and though the ex-Valencia man can play across the backline, White and Timber have rotated for the right-back slot, while Calafiori and Hincapie have shared left-back, leaving him with very few minutes since the start of the campaign.

Mosquera only signed last summer, but with ESPN reporting the transfer fee to be just £13 million, Arsenal may well consider flipping the 22-year-old for a steep profit, with the report claiming Arsenal want around £30m for his signature.

The champions also have a homegrown talent in the form of Marli Salmon, still just 17 years old but having already impressed both centrally and at right-back.

FourFourTwo understands that Arsenal have no interest in selling Mosquera in January but could reassess the situation next summer.

Mosquera is worth €40 million, according to Transfermarkt. Arsenal host Manchester City this weekend when Premier League action resumes.

#866. How a green economy could help reverse climate change

Green growth promises a future in which economies thrive without destroying the environment. But is this vision realistic?

Human civilization is currently profoundly unsustainable. Earth has already crossed seven of the nine planetary boundaries critical for sustaining life, including climate change, ocean acidification and biosphere integrity.

If economies and societies keep to business as usual, the Earth's vital processes will continue to be thrown wildly out of balance, threatening the future of humanity.

It's now largely accepted that if humans are to have any chance of slowing global warming and nature loss, those social and economic models must change. That's where the idea of green growth comes in.

Its promise is to keep growing the economy while reducing emissions and resource use. That involves, for instance, running factories, businesses and homes on wind, solar and other green energy instead of coal and gas, replacing gas-fired furnaces with heat pumps and  recycling and reusing resources and raw materials.

"Basically, the idea is: business as usual, but with more sustainable technologies," said Helmut Haberl, a social ecology professor at BOKU University in Vienna. Along with his colleagues, he published a major report in 2020 evaluating more than 800 studies on green growth.

In principle, the world's economic output could continue to grow in the long term and generate significantly fewer emissions from the burning of fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas. That's been shown in scenarios modeled by researchers with the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, or IPCC.

Thanks to renewable energy and green technologies, those scenarios have already become reality in several countries and regions.

The economies of developed countries like the United Kingdom, the United States, Japanand Australia have experienced years of growth alongside sinking CO2 emissions. That's even when offshore production is included.

In the European Union, the bloc-wide economy has grown by more than 70% since 1990. Meanwhile, the EU's carbon emissions have dropped by around 40%.

But such a complete decoupling of growth and emissions is, according to Haberl and his fellow researchers, relatively rare.

In India, and in several countries in Africa and Southeast Asia, economies are becoming more efficient. But while economic performance is outpacing emissions growth, emissions are still rising in those countries and globally. This is not compatible with preventing the worst impacts of climate change.

"That doesn't mean, however, that it couldn't work in the future," said Haberl, referring to decoupling of growth and emissions.

And even though economic growth has been shown to be compatible with emissions reduction, eliminating all greenhouse gases from a polluting industry like steel or chemicals is complicated.

These sectors don't just release emissions by burning fossil fuels for energy; carbon is also a key part of the chemical processes used to create their products, notably in the steel industry.

Replacing it with greener substitutes, or an alternative energy source like green hydrogen, requires significant investment.

There's another hurdle: the world's high consumption of resources. A productive economy depends on many raw materials and other products: ores, chemicals, wood, cement, glass and agricultural products.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Many countries are now using green technologies to reduce the amount of resources needed to manufacture a product, for example, and are making their economies more efficient.

But that doesn't mean overall fewer resources are being used because falling costs can encourage businesses to produce more things and people to consume more. This can partially offset green savings and is called the rebound effect.

The British economy has been growing for years, emissions have been dropping and efficiency has increased, but the UK still used 7% more resources in 2023 than it did in 2001.

Global resource consumption has tripled over the last 50 years. If the world continues on the current pathway, that could increase by another 60% by 2060. It remains unclear whether green growth can deliver the emissions and resource reductions needed to stop climate change and biodiversity loss rapidly enough.

"We really need to move beyond efficiency gains in our existing production practices to look more broadly at what we consume," said Catherine Ganzleben, a sustainability and fair transitions expert at the European Environment Agency.

She told DW that people also need to reconsider how they consume and whether they really need to own everything they use in their daily life — cars, for example.

"But we can shift towards models where we share cars, so we pool our resources and have significantly lower resources per person through sharing the goods that we need."

Some researchers have concluded that unrestricted economic growth is no longer possible in the long term, even if it's sustainable.

Instead, they've called for degrowth. This posits slower economic growth, no growth at all or even negative growth, so that the world's ecosystems and the climate have a chance to recover and stabilize.

That applies mainly to economies in richer countries, which would need to take targeted steps to reduce their energy and resource use. Poorer countries would continue to grow until their economies and quality of life improve significantly.

Under the degrowth theory, a society's prosperity is not measured solely by the growth of its gross domestic product, but by values such as quality of life, education and community. The idea is that once countries develop to a certain point, additional growth doesn't translate into greater well-being.

Ultimately, the concept is based on the idea that human well-being and ecological sustainability is only possible in the long term with a planned, socially just reduction of material production and resource consumption. Degrowth advocates argue this would be preferable to an unplanned and potentially catastrophic economic contraction caused by escalating climate extremes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

A 2020 study by researchers from the universities of Leeds and Lausanne showed that the concept of degrowth supported the world's climate goals — and that a high quality of life didn't have to be sacrificed in exchange for a significantly lower consumption of energy and resources.

However, there is still no conclusive evidence that an entire modern economy could continue to function entirely on the degrowth principles in the long term.

Nevertheless, Haberl doesn't assume that an environmentally friendly economic model automatically goes hand in hand with sacrifice, arguing instead for a needs-based economy.

"A society isn't necessarily better off when it's producing more goods and services," he said. It all depends on how prosperity and quality of life are measured in the future, and how states decide to do business.

Today, a successful economy is measured by the growth of a country's gross domestic product — put simply, the worth of all of its goods and services. This calculation doesn't account for income distribution, unpaid work, quality of life or environmental damage.

"The highest possible real incomes for every individual would probably not be compatible with ecological goals in the long term," said Haberl. "On the other hand, an increase in prosperity — related to a higher quality of life — would be."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

An analysis by the European Environment Agency (EEA) pointed out that the idea of steady growth is part of the world's economic cycle, and deeply anchored in our institutions, norms and societal discourse. The job market and tax system are also closely tied to gross domestic product growth. A shrinking economy would therefore require a fundamental shift in our way of thinking.

Countries face a dilemma: a steadily growing economy is not compatible with ecological goals, according to the EEA. On the other side, a sharp decline in growth could trigger enormous social upheaval.

And the correlation is much more complex than the idea of "less is more," as highlighted by an EEA study in November 2021. "The fact that GDP growth has been harmful for the environment does not necessarily mean that declining GDP would be good for the environment," noted the report.

Achieving green growth while respecting environmental limits would require an "unprecedented decoupling of economic activity from environmental and climate pressures. Whether this is feasible is currently uncertain."

This article was originally written in German.

New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino may well be about to address the dreaded left-back problem that has hampered the club for years

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Manchester United plan to address their issues at left-back by signing a player dubbed ‘the next Riccardo Calafiori’, following another poor result away at Sporting.

The Red Devils dropped two points in Europe last night away in Lisbon, with new manager Mauricio Pochettino winless in his first two games in charge, as the scale of the task at hand becomes clear.

With Manchester United 19th in both the Premier League and the Champions League's league phase right now, Pochettino is under pressure to deliver quickly, with January earmarked for much-needed new signings.

Once again, United have struggled at left-back this season, with veteran Luke Shaw injured for much of the campaign.

Lisandro Martinez started the 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino's first fixture, while Diogo Dalot has played out of position to cover there this term, with no obvious candidate to step in during Shaw's absence.

Sport Witness, however, have relayed a report from Gazzetta dello Sport, which claims that United have “already made moves” to sign Juan Miranda of Bologna.

The Spaniard signed for I Rossoblu following the sale of Riccardo Calafiori to Arsenal, and has impressed in Serie A with similar attacking instincts and reliable performances in manager Raffaele Palladino's backline.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

While Bologna are looking to tie Miranda down until 2030, there is significant interest from both Pochettino and Newcastle United, who see the 26-year-old as an option to alleviate the burden on Lewis Hall at left-back.

FourFourTwo understands that the Red Devils have a modest budget for January and may be limited in what they can do in the transfer market – meaning that cost-effective signings like Miranda may be the way forward, should Pochettino wish to strengthen.

After finishing third in the Premier League last season, manager Michael Carrick welcomed four new faces to Carrington in the form of Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans – all midfielders – and backup goalkeeper Karl Darlow, along with the returning Marcus Rashford, following his successful stint on loan with Barcelona.

While the lack of depth in defence and attack has been obvious this season though, United's midfield acquisitions have been questioned too for their lack of dynamism, with Carrick ultimately paying for the side's atrocious form with his job after just 10 league games.

United have won just three matches all season in all competitions.

Miranda is worth €15 million, according to Transfermarkt. Manchester United face Brentford this weekend when Premier League action resumes.

Terry Venables arrived at Middlesbrough in 2000 to work alongside manager Bryan Robson in an unconventional setup

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Mark Schwarzer has revealed that he feared a difficult reunion with Terry Venables when the former Australia manager arrived at Middlesbrough – only to find that the coach was willing to put their past disagreement behind them.

The pair had fallen out over Schwarzer’s availability for international duty in 1997, when the goalkeeper chose to honour a commitment to Boro rather than join an Australia squad under Venables.

Schwarzer had reason to worry about the potential for awkwardness when Venables was appointed to work alongside Bryan Robson at the Riverside in December 2000, tasked with helping Middlesbrough to beat the drop.

Schwarzer told FourFourTwo: “I was worried when Terry came in, because his previous job had been manager of Australia.

“I’d just joined Middlesbrough when we had that League Cup semi-final at the same time as an Australia call-up.

"Terry had made it clear that if he called you up, he expected you to be there

"Bryan Robson asked him if I could stay because it was one of the biggest games in Middlesbrough’s history.”

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

“Terry initially agreed, then three days beforehand called and said I had to choose. I told him I’d made a commitment to my club. He didn’t pick me again, including for the World Cup play-off against Iran.

“When he arrived at Middlesbrough, I wondered if there might be a problem. To his credit, he was brilliant. He basically said 'These things happen, let’s move on'."

Instead of allowing the dispute to linger, Schwarzer says Venables did a fantastic job of working out how to get Middlesbrough back in form

He said: “He made a huge impact at Middlesbrough. He spoke to everyone about what they thought was going wrong, then made his own mind up about how to address it.

“Terry was exceptional at not undermining Bryan. Robbo was still at the front of things but had this incredible coach to learn from. If Terry hadn’t come in, we would have been relegated.”

Boro eventually finished the 2000-01 Premier League season in 14th, well clear of the drop.

Fofana gave away a penalty during the 3-2 defeat at the City Ground and his own fans turned on him in a week where he gave a controversial, unauthorised interview

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Wesley Fofana had a night to forget for Chelsea at Nottingham Forest as he gave away a penalty and was booed by his own fans at the end of a week where he courted controversy.

The Blues defender, who has been singled out for poor performances during the team’s bad run, needed a strong showing, having spoken for almost two hours with French YouTuber Zack Nani on a range of topics in a controversial, unauthorised interview.

Fofana admitted that he came close to quitting football whilst he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate injury, while also appearing to joke about missing his penalty during last month’s Carabao Cup shootout defeat to Liverpool.

He apologised for the interview and boss Xabi Alonso said the matter was closed, but Friday’s Premier League game was a bad one for him.

The visiting supporters consistently jeered the centre-back when he was in possession in the first half. Fofana and his teammates endured a tough start at the City Ground as they fell behind to Igor Jesus’ brilliant fifth-minute strike.

A bad night got worse in the early stages of the second half when Fofana brought down Liam Delap for a penalty that Morgan Gibbs-White converted to double Forest’s lead.

He was substituted soon after, following chants from travelling Blues fans of “f*** off Fofana, you’re not wanted here.”

Emmanuel Emegha did score to halve the deficit but Gibbs-White’s second goal restored Forest’s healthy advantage and although another late Emegha strike saw the Blues pile on the pressure to try and snatch an injury-time equaliser, they ultimately suffered a 3-2 loss that their poor performance deserved.

Liverpool are beginning to see the very best of Florian Wirtz if recent form is anything to go by

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Florian Wirtz's £116 million Anfield arrival last summer was, on paper, a marquee addition to the Premier League, until he took to the field.

Supporters of all clubs were expectant, not least Liverpool fans. His debut campaign proved an awkward adaptation to English football, one in which the German seemed caught between systems, clearly in transition.

Fast forward to today and the player who lit up the Bundesliga with Bayer Leverkusen appears to have finally arrived on Merseyside.

Wirtz produced a standout display in Sunday’s 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United, where he scored an improvised goal to extend the Reds' lead and created 10 chances - albeit against 10 men - before finding the net again in Wednesday night’s 3-0 Champions League triumph over Club Brugge.

The underlying numbers from Gradient Sports prove this is no fleeting purple patch, either, especially after three goals in two games over the November international break.

According to Gradient Sports’ data, Wirtz’s overall player grade dipped sharply from a league-leading 91.0 in his final Bundesliga season with Leverkusen in 2024/25 to 73.1 during his debut 2025/26 Premier League campaign.

While his overall 2026/27 Premier League grade sits at 73.9, his attacking execution indicates a resurgence back toward his Leverkusen peak.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In the Premier League this season, Wirtz has had a 48 per cent increase in chances created - jumping from 1.99 to 2.94 per 90 minutes - ranking first among all Premier League wingers and attacking midfielders.

Even more telling is his cutting edge in the final third: Wirtz's passes directly leading to a half-chance have increased by 84 per cent, from 0.31 to 0.57 per 90.

His end product in front of goal tells a similar story. Gradient data notes that Wirtz’s positively graded shots have risen from 0.24 to 0.38 per 90 - closing in on the 0.45 he posted in 2024/25. Similarly, his 1.61 shots in the box per 90 actually surpasses his final Leverkusen tally of 1.60.

So, what has initiated the turnaround? New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola deserves credit for tweaking Wirtz's role and adjusting the team's tempo, but Anfield may also owe a debt of gratitude to Jurgen Klopp.

Since taking charge of the German national team, Klopp has turned Wirtz into his talisman; he has four goals in his last four international appearances. And it's that confidence which has bled into his club form, aided by private counsel from the former Reds manager. Wirtz revealed recently that he regularly speaks with Klopp about life at Anfield, taking on board "small, private things" from a man who knows exactly how to win over the Kop.

Armed with Klopp’s guidance and backed by the evidence of improved creative metrics in the Premier League, Liverpool’s £116m man is finally beginning to look worthy of his price tag.

#860. Xabi Alonso under huge pressure as Chelsea slip to dispiriting defeat at Nottingham Forest

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Nottingham Forest 3-2 Chelsea: Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice to help condemn the Blues to a third straight loss and Alonso’s job suddenly looks precarious

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Chelsea slumped to a third successive Premier League defeat as they went down 3-2 at Nottingham Forest to mount the pressure on boss Xabi Alonso.

The London club were second-best to Forest, who won it through Igor Jesus’ brilliant opener and a Morgan Gibbs-White double after the break.

Emmanuel Emegha scored twice to give the scoreline a different complexion, but that does not mask the overall poor performance.

The latest loss comes after last weekend’s alarming 4-1 defeat to Leeds and Alonso has clear issues to address as they slide down the table.

One of them is Wesley Fofana after the Frenchman was booed and jeered by his own fans after an unauthorised YouTube interview where he appeared to joke about the club’s Carabao Cup exit.

Forest claimed back-to-back home wins after beating Manchester City last time out at the City Ground and this performance was an indication that they are moving in the right direction under Oliver Glasner.

Alonso opted to change his defence after last week’s debacle against Leeds, dropping Levi Colwill and replacing him in the back four with midfielder Moises Caicedo. The Spaniard did stick with under-fire Fofana, who was booed from the off.

Both men came under early pressure as Forest began well. Liam Delap, desperate to score against the club where his career stalled last season, had a snap-shot in the first minute, but Emiliano Martinez was not troubled.

But the Argentina goalkeeper could do nothing about a sublime Forest opener in the fifth minute. Daniel Munoz drilled in a cross from that right that Jesus sent into the top corner with an acrobatic volley. It was a fine piece of athleticism, even if contact did come off the shin.

That was the only real moment of quality in a first half where Forest were the better side. Alonso’s men had nothing going forward and failed to muster a shot on target.

Things did not improve after the break as Fofana’s night got worse. He lost out on a routine challenge to Delap, who burst clear into the box and was felled by the Frenchman.

Referee Andy Madley pointed to the spot and Gibbs-White stepped up and sent Martinez the wrong way.

But Chelsea got themselves back into it three minutes later, with their first shot on target, and they needed plenty of luck.

Pedro Neto’s shot hit Jair Cunha and it fell kindly into the path of half-time substitute Emegha, who rifled into the bottom corner.

Fofana was then hooked as he was put out of his mercy, but Chelsea still looked vulnerable.

James McAtee should have done better with his shot after a fine pass by Gibbs-White, while Murillo’s thumping volley from distance brought a good save by Martinez.

Forest restored their two-goal cushion in the 72nd minute as they scored an excellent third. Xaver Schlager picked up a loose ball, made space with a fine first touch and then found Gibbs-White with an incisive pass, which the England international coolly clipped home.

They appeared to be seeing the match out with ease, but that changed in the 89th minute as Chelsea scored out of nothing.

Neto’s cross found Emegha who headed home to set up a grandstand finish, but Forest held on for a deserved three points.

England and Arsenal striker Alessia Russo speaks about football memories and handling pressure in front of goal as she partners with Lucozade

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Alessia Russo has two European Championships and a Champions League to her name and has established herself as one of England’s most prolific strikers.

In another impressive year for the 27-year-old, she became the highest-scoring English player in UEFA Women's Champions League history with a recent hat-trick against Benfica, was named England Women's Player of the Year and earned a place in the FIFPRO Women's World 11.

Speaking to former Three Lions striker Ian Wright at the launch of her new long-term partnership with Lucozade, the England and Arsenal forward discussed how she fell in love with football and the mentality behind her performances.

Russo grew up in Maidstone, Kent and football always featured in her life.

“Football has always been a massive part of my life,” she said. “Growing up, my dad would take me to watch women’s games at Charlton, and I remember looking up to those players and dreaming of doing the same one day.

“To see how far the game has come is incredible. Women’s football is now about so much more than what happens on the pitch. It’s influencing fashion, culture and bringing communities together in ways I could never have imagined growing up.

“To be part of that journey is really special.”

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Now one of the leading strikers in world football, Russo believes her calm approach is one of her biggest strengths when it comes to finding the back of the net.

"I've always been really laid back. I'm always wanting to win. Just because I'm not angry or shouting or screaming, doesn't mean I don't want to win and I don't want to score," she said.

"I think that calmness is something that I try and bring to the game. And I think as a striker, you have to be calm in and around the box. When things aren't going your way, I just kind of strip it back. I like to train hard and then whatever happens in the game happens.

"You can't control a whole lot as a No.9. You're quite reliant on other players. But what you can control is the moments that you do get."

The partnership will see Russo work with Lucozade Sport to better understand her individual hydration and fuelling requirements, with the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil on the horizon.

She will also help inform future product innovation as the brand continues its longstanding support of the Lionesses, dating back to 2006.
